title: Write a desugarer
starter:
type e =
  | Lit of float
  | Var of string
  | Add of e * e
  | Mul of e * e
  | Exp2 of e
  | Log2 of e
  | Sub of e * e
  | Exp of e
  | Log of e

let rec to_string = function
  | Lit x -> Printf.sprintf "%.7g" x
  | Var s -> s
  | Add (a, b) -> "(add " ^ to_string a ^ " " ^ to_string b ^ ")"
  | Mul (a, b) -> "(mul " ^ to_string a ^ " " ^ to_string b ^ ")"
  | Exp2 a -> "(exp2 " ^ to_string a ^ ")"
  | Log2 a -> "(log2 " ^ to_string a ^ ")"
  | Sub (a, b) -> "(sub " ^ to_string a ^ " " ^ to_string b ^ ")"
  | Exp a -> "(exp " ^ to_string a ^ ")"
  | Log a -> "(log " ^ to_string a ^ ")"

let rec desugar (e : e) : e =
  e
hints: Start with `match e with` and one branch per constructor. `Lit` and `Var` return `e` unchanged.
A core node rebuilds itself from desugared operands: `| Add (a, b) -> Add (desugar a, desugar b)`. Do the same for `Mul`, `Exp2` and `Log2`.
The sugar branches: `| Sub (a, b) -> Add (desugar a, Mul (desugar b, Lit (-1.0)))`, `| Exp a -> Exp2 (Mul (desugar a, Lit 1.442695))` and `| Log a -> Mul (Log2 (desugar a), Lit 0.6931472)`.

answer.code:
type e =
  | Lit of float
  | Var of string
  | Add of e * e
  | Mul of e * e
  | Exp2 of e
  | Log2 of e
  | Sub of e * e
  | Exp of e
  | Log of e

let rec to_string = function
  | Lit x -> Printf.sprintf "%.7g" x
  | Var s -> s
  | Add (a, b) -> "(add " ^ to_string a ^ " " ^ to_string b ^ ")"
  | Mul (a, b) -> "(mul " ^ to_string a ^ " " ^ to_string b ^ ")"
  | Exp2 a -> "(exp2 " ^ to_string a ^ ")"
  | Log2 a -> "(log2 " ^ to_string a ^ ")"
  | Sub (a, b) -> "(sub " ^ to_string a ^ " " ^ to_string b ^ ")"
  | Exp a -> "(exp " ^ to_string a ^ ")"
  | Log a -> "(log " ^ to_string a ^ ")"

let rec desugar (e : e) : e =
  match e with
  | Lit _ | Var _ -> e
  | Add (a, b) -> Add (desugar a, desugar b)
  | Mul (a, b) -> Mul (desugar a, desugar b)
  | Exp2 a -> Exp2 (desugar a)
  | Log2 a -> Log2 (desugar a)
  | Sub (a, b) -> Add (desugar a, Mul (desugar b, Lit (-1.0)))
  | Exp a -> Exp2 (Mul (desugar a, Lit 1.442695))
  | Log a -> Mul (Log2 (desugar a), Lit 0.6931472)
answer.explain: Every branch rebuilds its node from desugared operands, so the rewrite reaches the whole tree. The three sugar branches build their expansions: `sub a b` becomes `add a (mul b -1)`, `exp x` becomes `exp2 (mul x 1.442695)` and `log x` becomes `mul (log2 x) 0.6931472`. The result contains no sugar at all, so a later pass needs no cases for it.
